text:
elaine_pm: kicking off a PRD intake for a feature request from two regulated customers: they need verifiable response snapshots plus a redaction flow that preserves auditability. sketching problem + must-haves here.

mike_sre: 👍 can you list the perf/storage constraints up front? storing every response could blow up costs.

elaine_pm: agreed. core ask: 1) create an append-only snapshot per accepted response (metadata + optionally encrypted payload), 2) support a revocation API that redacts payload but records a tamper-proof revocation record, 3) expose audit queries and an export path for compliance teams.

sam_research: for replay/debugging we should include: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_id+version, prompt_hash, final_response_hash, response_blob(encrypted), tokens, timestamp, schema_version. streaming: only persist final committed output.

jordan_eng: couple of infra edgecases: high-QPS tenants -> sampling rules; very large blobs -> store pointer to object store; function-calls -> capture function name + args (encrypted) but allow redaction of args separately. need schema v1 that can extend.

tara_prod: non-goals: full-text indexing / search of blobs in alpha; exporting every snapshot to analytics. we'll support metadata search only.

olivia_legal: compliance notes: revocation must be auditable: record who requested it (actor id), timestamp, reason, and method. When redaction happens, plaintext must be unrecoverable from the snapshot store, but revocation record must show proof of action. chain-of-custody log required.

mike_sre: ops options: (A) store all metadata in DB + blobs in encrypted object store with per-tenant KMS, (B) default sampling: metadata for all, full blob only when flagged or size<threshold. prefer async ingestion so we never block API response path.

sam_research: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- config: tenant.settings.revocable_snapshots boolean + route override boolean
- snapshot write: returns snapshot_id before ingestion completes; snapshot.status = ingested|failed|pending
- revocation API: POST /v1/snapshots/:id/revoke {actor, reason} -> stores immutable revocation record; snapshot.payload replaced with <REDACTED_v1> token; revocation record includes actor, timestamp, reason, revocation_id
- audit API: GET /v1/snapshots?tenant=&from=&to= returns metadata + revocation state; payload only if allowed by tenant key and not redacted
- streaming: snapshot recorded at commit point, not intermediate chunks
- perf: enabling snapshots for a test tenant with default sampling must keep p95 latency increase <5%

jordan_eng: implementation plan notes: writer service to accept snapshot events (idempotent), object-store plugin for encrypted blobs, revocation service that atomically swaps pointer -> redaction token, audit-log append-only in write-once storage. need migrations and versioning.

olivia_legal: also require retention policies UI (90/180/360 days) + explicit delete policy when tenant requests complete deletion; deletion must create an audit entry showing deletion request and result.

elaine_pm: success metrics for alpha: onboard 3 pilot customers; avg audit query latency <200ms for typical queries; revocation operation visible in console within 5s; no security/compliance fail in first 6 months.

mike_sre: questions to answer in RFC: do we offer per-tenant KMS in phase-1 or managed keys only? fallback behavior if object-store write is slow (queue + retry vs sync fallback). SLA implications for snapshot availability.

sam_research: risks & mitigations: PII risk -> tenant KMS + envelope encryption; cost risk -> sampling + retention slider defaults; operational risk -> feature-gated rollout and canary on low-volume tenants.

infra-bot: note: add security review + threat model before design review.

elaine_pm: next steps: I'll draft the PRD and RFC with acceptance criteria above and a phased rollout: alpha (managed keys, sampling defaults, metadata search only), beta (per-tenant KMS, full blobs selectable), GA (longer retention, exports). please comment if you want to be co-owner (esp. @olivia_legal and @mike_sre).
